title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Quarter-Wave Initialization at Methane Band Center
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses to quarter-wave optical thickness at the methane passband center (3.30 μm) rather than uniform random values will provide a physically meaningful starting point that accelerates convergence toward high transmittance in both passbands while maintaining stopband suppression.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack principle: alternating high/low index layers with optical thickness λ/4 at design wavelength creates constructive interference for reflection at that wavelength. For dual-band transmission, thicknesses must be optimized away from pure quarter-wave to create transmission windows at both target bands.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 substrate (22 finite layers total, alternating sequence starting with ZnS)
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses in nm, initialized to quarter-wave values at 3300 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds [50, 950] nm prevent optimizer saturation
ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for alternating index multilayers
Transfer matrix method for coherent thin-film interference
expected_advantages: Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Bounded thickness prevents optimizer from hitting upper boundary prematurely
22 layers provide sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
known_risks: Quarter-wave at one band may not generalize well to second passband
May require more optimization iterations to escape local minimum
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate with alternating ZnS (high index) and MgF2 (low index) layers under normal unpolarized illumination. Initialize all 22 layer thicknesses to quarter-wave optical thickness at 3300 nm center wavelength (ZnS: n*thickness = 3300/4 nm, MgF2: n*thickness = 3300/4 nm using material refractive indices). Constrain all thicknesses to [50, 950] nm bounds. Use gradient-based thickness optimization to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm) while minimizing mean transmittance in stopbands (2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm). Evaluate using coherent transfer matrix method across 2500-5000 nm wavelength range. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Replaced uniform random thickness initialization with deterministic quarter-wave estimates at methane band center (3300 nm) per feedback directive; capped maximum thickness at 950 nm to prevent optimizer saturation at 1100 nm boundary
